_about: The workshop's component library, shared by the browser (simulator, schematic, 3D) and the server (app/tools/workshop_project.py: checks, bill of materials). Each type: label, kind, the catalog item it is bought as (exact names from app/data/latech_*.psv, or online_parts.psv where campus has nothing for the job), pins (name -> role), props with defaults, size in mm [x, y, z] (z up), and the electrical figures the checks use. need: pins that must be wired for the part to work. draw_ma: typical current from its supply pin. Sizes marked approx should be measured before a tight print.

rgb_led.label: RGB LED (common cathode)
rgb_led.note: The vending machine's RGB LED does not say common cathode or anode; check with a meter.

servo.label: Continuous-rotation micro servo (FS90R)
servo.note: Every servo Tech stocks is continuous rotation: write(90) stops it, below 90 turns one way, above the other. A positional (0-180 degree) servo is not stocked.

dc_motor.label: N20 mini gear motor
dc_motor.catalog: Motor: mini gear motor, N20, metal gears

fan.label: 2 in. 12V fan
fan.catalog: Fan, 2" square; 12VDC x 3/8"; T&T box fan

stepper.label: NEMA 17 stepper motor
stepper.catalog: Motor: NEMA 17 stepper motor (no motor controller)

a4988.label: A4988 stepper driver
a4988.catalog: A4988 motor driver (ENGR 122 & NEMA stepper motor)

hall.label: Digital hall sensor (open collector)
hall.catalog: Hall effect sensor (non-latching digital, unipolar, incl magnet)
hall.note: OUT only pulls low when the magnet is near; it needs a pull-up (INPUT_PULLUP or a 10k to 5V).

adxl335.label: ADXL335 3-axis accelerometer
adxl335.note: Runs on 3.3V (the UNO's 3V3 pin), not 5V. Outputs about 1.65V at 0 g, 0.33V per g.

breadboard_400.label: Breadboard, 400 tie-point
breadboard_400.catalog: Breadboard: 400 tie-point (120 robot; may incl mounting holes)

ball_caster.label: Ball caster, 1 in.
ball_caster.catalog: Ball caster w/ 1" plastic ball and plastic rollers

lead_screw.label: T8x2 lead screw and nut
lead_screw.catalog: Lead screw (threaded rod) with T8x2 nut, 300mm

esp32.label: WEMOS ESP32 board (D1 R32)
esp32.note: ESP32 with WiFi and Bluetooth, on the UNO-shaped WEMOS D1 R32 board (confirm the store's board; the GPIO numbers are the same on every WEMOS ESP32). 3.3V logic: never put 5V on a pin. Analog reads only on IO32-IO39 while WiFi is on; IO34-IO39 are inputs only. Program it in the Arduino IDE with the ESP32 core (board: ESP32 Dev Module). Not simulated live: its wiring and code are checked.

feather_s3.label: Adafruit ESP32-S3 Feather
feather_s3.catalog: Adafruit ESP32-S3 Feather (4MB flash, 2MB PSRAM, LiPo charger + MAX17048 fuel gauge, USB-C)
feather_s3.note: Small ESP32-S3 board for worn builds: WiFi + Bluetooth LE, USB-C, a LiPo charger on board (plug the cell into its JST: wired here to BAT and GND) and a MAX17048 fuel gauge on its I2C. USB is live only while plugged in; BAT is the cell (3.0-4.2V). 3.3V logic. Program it in the Arduino IDE (board: Adafruit Feather ESP32-S3 2MB PSRAM). Not simulated live: its wiring and code are checked.

servo_micro.label: MG90S positional micro servo (180 deg, metal gear)
servo_micro.catalog: MG90S Micro Servo, Metal Gear (180 degree)
servo_micro.note: Positional: write(angle) holds 0-180 degrees. 2.0 kg-cm at 4.8V. Every campus servo is continuous rotation, so this one is ordered online.

servo_std.label: MG996R positional servo (180 deg, high torque)
servo_std.catalog: MG996R Servo, Metal Gear, High Torque (180 degree)
servo_std.note: Positional, 9 kg-cm at 4.8V; stalls at about 2.5A, so it needs its own 5-6V supply - never a board's 5V pin.

lipo_500.label: LiPo cell 3.7V 500mAh
lipo_500.note: Protected 1-cell LiPo, 3.7V nominal (4.2V full, cut-off 3.0V). Charge only on a LiPo charger at 500 mA or less.

lipo_1200.label: LiPo cell 3.7V 1200mAh
lipo_1200.note: Protected 1-cell LiPo, 3.7V nominal. Charge only on a LiPo charger at 500 mA or less.

lipo_2500.label: LiPo cell 3.7V 2500mAh
lipo_2500.note: Protected 1-cell LiPo, about 9 Wh. Charge only on a LiPo charger.

lipo_charger.label: Micro-Lipo charger, USB-C
lipo_charger.catalog: Adafruit Micro-Lipo Charger, USB Type C
lipo_charger.note: Charges a 1-cell LiPo from any USB-C cable: 100 mA as shipped, 500 mA with its jumper closed. Red LED charging, green full. 5V is live only while plugged in.

boost_5v.label: MiniBoost 5V 1A (TPS61023)
boost_5v.note: Lifts a LiPo's 3.0-4.2V to a steady 5V: about 1.1A from a 3.7V cell (less as it runs down).

fuel_gauge.label: MAX17048 LiPo fuel gauge
fuel_gauge.catalog: Adafruit MAX17048 LiPoly / LiIon Fuel Gauge and Battery Monitor
fuel_gauge.note: Reads the cell's voltage and charge in percent over I2C (address 0x36). BAT goes to the cell's +; on an UNO, SDA is A4 and SCL A5.

mic_amp.label: MAX9814 electret mic amplifier (auto gain)
mic_amp.catalog: Electret Microphone Amplifier - MAX9814 with Auto Gain Control
mic_amp.note: Microphone with automatic gain control: its OUT is an audio signal (1.25V bias, up to 2Vpp) for an amplifier's input or an analog pin.

audio_amp.label: PAM8302 2.5W mono amplifier
audio_amp.catalog: Adafruit Mono 2.5W Class D Audio Amplifier - PAM8302
audio_amp.note: Analog audio in (A+, with A- to ground for a single-ended source), 2.5W into a 4-8 ohm speaker. SD low mutes it (pulled high on the board). Volume on its trim pot.

i2s_amp.label: MAX98357A I2S 3W amplifier
i2s_amp.catalog: Adafruit I2S 3W Class D Amplifier Breakout - MAX98357A
i2s_amp.note: Digital (I2S) audio straight from an ESP32 into a speaker: 3.2W into 4 ohm at 5V. Not for the UNO: I2S needs the ESP32.

speaker.label: Enclosed speaker 3W 4 ohm
speaker.note: 4 ohm, 3W, in its own box (JST-PH lead). Drive it from an amplifier's SPK+/SPK-, never a board pin.

fan_5v.label: 30mm 5V fan
fan_5v.catalog: Miniature 5V Cooling Fan for Raspberry Pi (30x30x8mm, 0.2A)
fan_5v.note: Brushless 5V fan, 0.2A. Switch it with a logic-level MOSFET on its - lead (PWM for speed) and a flyback diode across it.

pulse_sensor.label: Pulse Sensor Amped (heart rate)
pulse_sensor.note: Optical heart-rate sensor for a fingertip or ear lobe: S is an analog waveform (half the supply at rest) with a peak each beat. Run it from 3.3V on an ESP32.

neopixel_ring12.label: NeoPixel ring, 12 RGB
neopixel_ring12.catalog: NeoPixel Ring - 12 x 5050 RGB LED with Integrated Drivers
neopixel_ring12.note: 12 addressable RGB LEDs on one data pin (Adafruit_NeoPixel). About 60 mA each at full white; 120 mA at a typical brightness. Put about 200 ohm in series with DIN.

neopixel_stick8.label: NeoPixel stick, 8 RGB
neopixel_stick8.catalog: NeoPixel Stick - 8 x 5050 RGB LED with Integrated Drivers
neopixel_stick8.note: 8 addressable RGB LEDs in a row; chain sticks DOUT to DIN. Bright enough to read in daylight. Put about 200 ohm in series with DIN.

pir.label: PIR motion sensor (SparkFun, JST)
pir.note: Sees a person moving up to about 7 m away; AL is open collector and goes LOW on motion, so use INPUT_PULLUP or a 10k pull-up. Give it 1-2 s to settle at power-on.

vibe_motor.label: Vibration motor 1.5-4.5V
vibe_motor.note: Buzzes for haptic feedback. 80 mA: switch it with a MOSFET (or NPN), with a flyback diode across it.

supply_5v4a.label: 5V 4A power supply
supply_5v4a.note: Wall brick with a 2.1 mm barrel plug: wire it through the screw-terminal jack adapter. 5V only - it cannot feed an UNO's barrel jack (that needs 7V+), so it goes to 5V pins and servo rails.

speaker_thin.label: Thin speaker 0.5W 8 ohm (40 mm)
speaker_thin.note: Flat 40 mm speaker, 4.5 mm deep: fits behind a grille in a thin wall. 0.5W - keep a PAM8302 at 5V turned well down (its trim pot), it can give 1.5W into 8 ohm.
